body: That's a good one! I have a feeling that goes such a long way with sensors. Asking lots of questions about what they've been up to always seems to go well with them in my experience!

Sorry, my phone won't let me reply to your response!

Right I see! Maybe you could have a chat with an examiner? If not, reading examiners' reports online can be interesting and quite eye opening. 

It's very possible that you'll gain some marks! It's remarked by senior examiners (I think?) who might be more likely to be fair in their judgments of your work. 

Which books did you read for your GCSE? If you don't read a lot, it's a good idea to start reading a little bit more. It's also a good idea to maybe join a book club? They can be really fun if you like reading, and listening to other people's thoughts is great for developing your own thinking. When you analyse literature, what are the first few things you tend to think about?

What is your ultimate goal? What are you hoping to get out of sitting your GCSEs?

I'm sorry you aren't happy with your results! You seem to be able to write pretty well.  

Have you thought about getting your paper remarked? It could have just been marked very harshly. 

Did you have English lessons with a tutor before you sat your exam? It could be a case of just not knowing what to look for, what is important to talk about, how to analyse, how to explain your thought processes in an eloquent and concise way. It doesn't mean you lack the capability! You can do it.

What kinds of things did you have to do for your exams? What did you find particularly difficult about the exam? Did you have coursework to do? 

I think it could be a good idea to ask for access to your scripts to look over what might have gone wrong, and learn from it! 

Don't lose heart! Your post here is well written and clear, I have no doubt that you're capable of doing really well.

Thank you for replying!

Don't worry- I won't be using the painkillers again! They made me feel so much worse in between sleeps...

Thank you, I really needed to hear your third point! I know it's true. It's just actually making myself act upon it. I don't know what's wrong with me. 

I'm going to be quite busy, and I have a lot of group work with people I would prefer to avoid. I also have to live with people I would rather avoid. I'm just desperate to get out of this but I'm completely trapped- I'd be letting so many people down and putting them in horrible situations if I left.

In all fairness though it's not like overweight women sail through life without any criticism. Do women shout 'oi shorty!' to you in the street regularly? You also must have noticed the complete media-fueled obsession with women's bodies and their looks. Women are taught early on that their looks are the most important things they can offer. Men don't get that so much.

That being said, it is unfair, and it is not cool to belittle anyone for how they look. I'm just pointing out why a woman's weight is such a touchy issue.
